Grade 9 • Lebanese Curriculum

Remarkable Identities

Visual lesson on expanding and simplifying using the three remarkable identities, with real-life situations, animation, mini explainer clips, drag-and-drop and challenge questions.

1. Before the identities: expanding

The lesson first reminds us that:

k(a + b) = ka + kb

This distributive property is the starting point for developing products.

3(x + 4)
3(x + 4)
= 3 × x + 3 × 4
= 3x + 12
Remarkable identities are special shortcuts for products that appear very often.

2. Identity 1: square of a sum

(a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b²
a²
ab
ab
b²

The large square is divided into a², ab, ab and b², so its total area is a² + 2ab + b².

(a + b)²

3. Real-life situation: enlarging a square garden

A square garden has side a. A strip of width b is added to the right and bottom, making a larger square of side a + b.

(a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b²

If a = 6 m and b = 2 m, find the new area.



4. Identity 2: square of a difference

(a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b²
First term squared: a²
Minus twice the product: −2ab
Second term squared: +b²
(a − b)²

5. Identity 3: difference of two squares

(a − b)(a + b) = a² − b²
(a − b)(a + b)
= a² + ab − ab − b²
= a² − b²

Quick calculation:

59 × 61 = (60 − 1)(60 + 1)
= 60² − 1² = 3599
